text:
Alex: quick sync: proposal for a 'consensus fallback' layer to reconcile competing triggers (canary, AB metric, semantic guard) before routing flips.
Priya: interested. current problem: multiple systems can trigger fallback and we get flappy double-swaps. what's the core idea?
Alex: short: introduce a lightweight arbitration service that ingests candidate actions (who wants to flip, why, weight) and emits a single canonical decision per route/time-window.
Jonah: sounds heavier than existing router rules. how is this different from 'priority order'?
Alex: because priority order is brittle. arbitration can combine signals, apply rate-limits, cooldowns, and seek minimal-impact remediation (partial percentage shift, shadow, full cut). also supports delay windows to collect additional telemetry.
Lin: example flow?
Alex: event sources: canary.monitor, perf.slo, semantic.guard. each posts a candidate: {action: 'fallback', reason:'semantic_drop', confidence:0.82, suggested_pct:100, owner:'semantic.guard'}. arbitrator waits up to N ms or until min_samples, then resolves.
Priya: resolution policy? deterministic and auditable please.
Alex: propose policy steps: 1) quick vetoes: infra errors/timeouts -> immediate failover. 2) if multiple fallbacks same window: merge by selecting smallest common action that satisfies safety (e.g., prefer partial traffic diversion if safe). 3) if one signal has high confidence (>0.9) and others low, take high-confidence. 4) otherwise, request shadowing + wait-window (default 30s) and then promote.
Jonah: how to compute 'confidence'? different detectors produce different scales.
Lin: normalize to [0,1] with per-signal calibration curve. store calibration metadata in the model registry.
Priya: cooldown/hysteresis? Also avoid oscillation across multiple tenants on same route.
Alex: per-route cool down + global rate limit. defaults: cooldown=10m, tenant-global-safety-lock if >5% tenants flip same minute. also track recent decisions to bias towards stability (decay function).
Jonah: operator ergonomics? simple APIs and visible trail please.
Alex: arbitration API: POST /arbitrate {route, candidate_actions[]} returns decision {action, applied_pct, reason, trace_id}. Every decision emits an event to event-bus and populates console timeline.
Lin: what about canaries that intentionally ramp? we mustn't block deliberate progressive ramps.
Alex: include 'intent' flag in candidate: {intent:'ramp', autoroll:false}. Arbitrator respects explicit operator-intent (bypasses some auto rules) but still can veto on hard infra failure. Also supports 'guardrails-as-code' to opt routes into stricter arbitration.
Priya: observability: need to see what lost the arbitration and why.
Jonah: yes, console: decision trace UI, side-by-side metric snapshots at decision time, and a sample diff when safe variant used. exportable for postmortems.
Lin: performance: added latency in decision loop?
Alex: keep arbitration window short (default 250ms) for fast events; for uncertain cases we let detectors post 'deferred mode' decisions which trigger wait-window (30s). System must scale horizontally; decisions are idempotent and cached.
Priya: data privacy: candidates may point to sample outputs. ensure scrub + rate-limit when publishing events.
Jonah: test plan?
Alex: unit: policy combinator tests. integration: simulate concurrent signals using chaos harness. pilot: 2 internal services + 1 external tenant for 3 weeks. KPIs: reduction in flip churn (>50%), mean time to mitigation <= 60s, false-positive rate <=2%.
Lin: failure modes: arbitrator outage -> fallback to simple priority order with strict timeouts. we should implement a safe default in router.
Alex: yes fallback behavior encoded as router 'local-autonomy' mode: if no decision returned within X ms, router uses local priority and emits a degrade-warning.
Priya: roll-out steps?
Alex: RFC -> implement API + console trace -> internal-only pilot -> opt-in for additional tenants -> global enable. feature-flag everything.
Jonah: SLOs for arbitrator? uptime 99.95 and p99 decision latency <300ms.
Alex: ops/playbook: add recovery steps, how to force-apply decisions, and oncall escalation when >3 arbitration errors in 1h.
Lin: small ask: expose a 'simulator' endpoint so teams can feed hypothetical candidate sets and see what decision would be made.
Alex: good idea. will add.
Priya: thumbs up. can you draft the RFC with policy grammar, example candidates, and console mocks?
Alex: will do. adding stakeholders: Priya, Jonah, Lin, Platform-SRE.
rollout-bot: arbitration-service v0.1 deployed to staging at 2025-01-09T12:03:00Z (build 1.0.0)
